# Skill: lean-update

# lean-update

The script (`lean-agents`, `scripts/lean.mjs`) is the only thing that changes files: deterministic, tested, undone by `--uninstall`. You are the middleware: detect, ask, run it, read it back. Change nothing before the user says yes.

Run the script with `npx -y lean-agents@<version> <flags>` (the latest release version, below). Without npm access or Node.js 22.20+, use the fallback bootstrap. It checks git and Node.js the way the README does (`install.sh` offers `brew install` only with Homebrew, asks first, else stops with a link; `install.ps1` uses `winget`), then downloads that release and checks its SHA256: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/releases/download/<tag>/install.sh | bash -s -- <flags>`. In a clone, `node scripts/lean.mjs ...` works too. Use the latest release tag: `gh release view --repo estebanmr99/lean-agents --json tagName -q .tagName`. When `LEAN_AGENTS_RELEASE_DIR` is set, read `package.json`, `core/pins.json` and `CHANGELOG.md` from that directory instead, use its `version` as the latest tag, and skip the `gh` and raw GitHub fetches.

1. **Read the release.** Fetch `core/pins.json` at that tag from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/<tag>/`. Then read every release between the installed lean-agents version (`version` in `state.json`; for a hand install, ask or say it is unknown and read from the oldest release you can match) and the latest: `gh release view <tag> --repo estebanmr99/lean-agents --json body -q .body`, and the matching `CHANGELOG.md` sections. A pin's `note` adds to the impact.
   - Start your answer with the **breaking changes and upgrade steps** from those notes, before any table.
   - The notes mention OpenCode 2: say that upgrading OpenCode is the user's own step (lean-agents never upgrades it), and that before it they should back up the OpenCode data folder (`opencode.db`) and config; see "Staying on OpenCode 1.x" in `docs/compatibility.md`. This skill never runs the OpenCode upgrade.
   - A release with no clear "Upgrade" or "Breaking" notes: say so in plain words, and put "none in the release notes" in the table.
2. **Detect.**
   - `~/.config/lean-agents/state.json` exists (or `--doctor --json` works): run `--doctor --json`. Its `behind` list is what is older than the pins.
   - No `state.json` (installed by hand): run the read-only commands in "Detect what is installed" in `docs/manual-install.md` to learn which agents and tools are there. Say that this install has no state yet and that the script will take it over without overwriting user files.
3. **Dry run as JSON, with the script.**
   - With state: `--update --dry-run --yes --json`.
   - Without state: `--dry-run --yes --json --agents <detected> --tools <detected>`.
   The JSON lists files, commands (exact `npx`/`brew` lines, all pinned) and, on update, `behind`. When the user asked to update everything and an Orca or Warp app is older than its pin, pass `--install-terminal orca|warp|both` on the dry run and the real run: non-interactively that is the only way a user-installed app is adopted and updated.
4. **Show one table** in plain words: `tool | installed | pinned | impact | upgrade notes | what it would run`. Installed comes from `behind` or the detection; impact from step 1 ("not in the changelog" when it is not); upgrade notes from the releases in step 1 ("none in the release notes" when there are none); what it would run from the JSON `commands`. Then, as its own last line, ask the question word for word: `Update these N tools?` (N is the number of rows in the table). Add nothing after it and ask no other question in that message. Stop on no.
5. **Back up only what changes, then run.** One backup folder in the OS temp directory holding the files the JSON says will change (paths start with `~`: expand them to full paths first) and that the engine does not already restore. This snippet is proven in bash only; its embedded quotes are **untested on PowerShell 5.1**, so on Windows PowerShell save the same JavaScript to a `.js` file in the temp folder and run `node <file> <path1> <path2>` instead. It prints the folder and copies each path in as `<n>-<name>`: `node -e "const fs=require('fs'),os=require('os'),p=require('path');const d=fs.mkdtempSync(p.join(os.tmpdir(),'lean-agents-backup-'));process.argv.slice(1).forEach((f,i)=>{if(fs.existsSync(f))fs.cpSync(f,p.join(d,i+'-'+p.basename(f)),{recursive:true})});console.log(d)" <path1> <path2>`. Then run the same flags without `--dry-run`: `--update --yes`, or `--yes --agents ... --tools ...`.
   - From an agent's terminal there is no TTY: after the user approves the dry run, always pass `--yes` on the real run.
   - If the run refuses because an `opencode` process is running: when the refusal names `opencode service stop` (outside OpenCode), run that command once, then retry the run once. When it says "you are running inside OpenCode", stop, never run `opencode service stop` (it stops the service your own session runs on), and give the user the terminal command it names.
   - Stop at the first failure: write the redacted draft (step 7) and report it, instead of trying workarounds such as removing a plugin marketplace.
6. **Read it back.** Run `--doctor --json`. When `ok` is true and `behind` is empty, delete the backup folder (same PowerShell 5.1 caveat: use a `.js` file there) with `node -e "require('fs').rmSync(process.argv[1],{recursive:true,force:true})" <folder>` and tell the user it is gone and that `--uninstall` still undoes everything. When it is not, keep the backup, say where it is, and offer to restore.
   - **Hand-off:** if this lean-agents release offers the finish-step summary page (#181), tell the user it exists and offer to open it after they agree; the page lists what was updated, kept and skipped and the logins still needed. If this release has no such page, skip this and go to step 8.
7. **Share findings (optional).** Only if you found a problem or an improvement (a failed command, a tool the detection cannot see, a missing changelog note):
   - Never offer under `--privacy strict`, `--network off` or `--outbound off`. Read the saved preset from `state.json`; with no state, ask once whether outbound calls are allowed.
   - Ask: "Draft a redacted issue for lean-agents?" Stop on no.
   - `lean-agents --feedback-draft --feedback-kind update --failed-command "<tool>" --network on` with the details on stdin (bash: `< details.txt`; PowerShell: `Get-Content details.txt | npx -y lean-agents@<version> ...`). `{"offer": false}` means stop.
   - Duplicates: `gh issue list --repo estebanmr99/lean-agents --search "<title words>"`. If one matches, show it and stop.
   - Show the full draft. Only after a yes: `gh issue create --repo estebanmr99/lean-agents --title "<title>" --body-file <draft>`.
8. **Report**: old -> new per tool, what you verified (`--doctor --json`), what is left for the user.

## Fallback: the script cannot run

Only when Node is missing or the machine blocks the script. Use the table of commands and the install lines in `docs/manual-install.md` (sections 4, 6, 7) by hand, with the same table, the same ask, the same backup and the same read-back. Say that this is the fallback: nothing here is recorded in `state.json`, so `--uninstall` will not know about it.

# Changelog

All notable changes are documented here. Format: [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/). Versioning: [SemVer](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

## [1.2.5] - 2026-11-27

### Added
- `scripts/release-gate.sh <version> [sha]` runs the release gate (audit headings, open `audit` issues, green `ci.yml` run) locally, and `release.yml` calls it instead of inline steps (#515).
- Changelog fragments: each PR adds `changes/<issue>.md`; `node scripts/changelog.mjs <version>` folds them into `CHANGELOG.md` in the release PR, so parallel PRs no longer conflict under `## [Unreleased]` (#516).

### Changed
- `core/AGENTS.md` trimmed from 3,016 to 1,599 bytes; every 1.2.4 safety rule kept (#532)

### Docs
- `docs/audit-template.md` with the headings a release audit must have (#515)

### Fixed
- Real-binary CI downloads retry a 5xx three times before failing (#505)
- `--adopt` and `--upgrade-agent` shorten a Windows home path to `~` whatever its letter case, and `tilde()` no longer matches a home inside a longer path (#506)

## [1.2.4] - 2026-11-27

### Added
- `--adopt` (and `--adopt --json`) now lists every global npm package under every Node nvm knows, not only the npm packages lean-agents pins (#465). The active/default Node is marked, and a package is flagged when it exists only under another Node (`not-active`), sits under several Nodes at different versions (`version-differs`) or does not meet its own `engines.node` on the Node it lives under (`engines-unmet`). Cleanup is one `npm uninstall -g <pkg> --prefix <Node dir>` line per package only on a non-active Node: printed, never run, and not part of the `--yes` plan. The `--adopt --json` shape is in `docs/adopt-json.md`. nvm-windows stays **VERIFY**. Not done yet: flagging MCP/hook entries on a non-active Node and listing Node installs outside nvm on PATH.
- Multi-agent benchmark harness (#404): `tests/bench-multiagent.mjs` runs task9 solo or split across 1, 2 or 4 workers plus one reviewer, records per-session tokens and wall time, and reports priced cost and cost versus solo. It has a `--dry-run` plan, a hard USD cap, and a manual-only workflow.

### Fixed
- The Claude Code `context-mode` plugin pin moved from `v2.1.4` to `v2.1.7`, matching the npm CLI that `--update` already installs (#490). A new test fails when the two pins drift apart without a `note` on the plugin pin explaining why.
- The skipped `real-vscode-others` job no longer shows an unexpanded `real-vscode (${{ matrix.os }})` name in the checks list (#460). It has no custom name now, so a skip should show `real-vscode-others` and a real run still shows one job per OS.
- `--doctor` clears a stale `~/.claude/settings.json` hash left by 1.2.1, when the only difference is keys lean-agents' own `claude plugin` commands wrote (`enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`): `--update` now refreshes the stored hash for tracked JSON files whose command-written key paths it knows, even when the file did not change in that run (#492). A key lean-agents does not write still shows "edited since install".

## [1.2.3] - 2026-11-26

### Changed
- Quieter output (#491): each install or `--update` step prints one line `[n/N] description ✓` (or `✗` with the last 20 lines and the log path); the commands' own output goes to one log per run in `~/.config/lean-agents/logs/` (removed by `--uninstall`), so a child's stderr no longer shows red in PowerShell on a good run. The plan lists only `create`/`modify`/`remove` files plus one `N unchanged` line, release notes show the first sentence of each entry plus the CHANGELOG link, and command lines print the home as `~`. `--verbose` restores the full output; `--json` is unchanged. Child commands get no stdin, so a tool that asks a question takes its default instead of waiting (#489).

### Added
- `--preflight` (and `--preflight --json`) is a read-only check for old or duplicate copies of the agent CLIs and tools on PATH and for a terminal opened before a PATH change (#471). It lists every copy and which one wins, and gives one fix line per finding. Blockers (exit 1): rtk below its minimum version (its steps are skipped), a newer copy hidden behind an older one, a tool this window cannot see yet. Everything else, such as an older copy later on PATH, uv, jq or gh below their verified version, or a CLI behind its pinned version, is a warning. It only runs `--version` (and `reg.exe query` on Windows); `--no-exec` skips both. It also lists the OpenCode MCP server names (your own as `<user-mcp-N>`, so the report can be shared), warns when a pinned npm tool sits under several nvm Nodes or only under an inactive one (#465), and blocks when the disk is too small for the OpenCode 1.x backup or an OpenCode process is running (#488). jq and the other tools get a package-manager fix line.

### Fixed
- `--adopt` no longer marks a skill as `duplicate` when lean-agents installed it and every copy is the same (#477), for example `lean-update` after an install for Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code Copilot, or `orca-cli` with `--terminal orca`. The Skills CLI writes one copy per agent folder on purpose. So `--adopt --yes --confirm-removals` no longer offers to remove those copies. Copies that differ, or a skill from a failed install, are still flagged. `--doctor` already worked this way.
- The Copilot CLI context-mode step no longer uses a `context-mode` copy in the current folder. That happened when `npm root -g` failed. It now uses only absolute paths and otherwise stops with the "not found" message.
- `--feedback-draft` titles say "Problem running: …" instead of "Install failed" (the input can be a warning from a command that exited 0), and a long title ends on a whole word with `…` (#476). Package specs such as `lean-agents@1.2.1` stay in the draft (fixed by the redaction change in #491; now tested).
- Child processes no longer run in shell mode (#475, Node 24 warning DEP0190). Arguments with a space, `&`, `%` or `|` now reach the program unchanged, Windows npm and npx included (their `.cmd` files run through `cmd.exe` with each argument quoted, as cross-spawn does it).
- `--doctor` and the step lines no longer print your full Windows home path when a path uses another letter case than the home folder (`c:\Users\...` for Copilot files, #493): it shows `~\...` like every other row, so pasted output does not carry your username. macOS and Linux stay case-sensitive.
- `--doctor`'s DCP row reads OpenCode 2.2.7's plugin cache (`~/.cache/opencode/npm/<pkg>@<spec>/<id>/`), so it no longer shows an old `resolved` version and a false "changed" while the pinned DCP loads fine (#495). `--doctor --probe-plugins` copies only what the probe needs (not the config's `node_modules` or wrappers of specs the config no longer asks for), so it no longer stops at the size cap on a long-used cache.
- `--update` refuses to start, and changes nothing, when its plan touches OpenCode (the CLI upgrade, `rtk init --opencode`, the GSD install for OpenCode) while an `opencode` process runs: the 1.x app or the 2.x background service. It says to run `opencode service stop` first (#488). `--dry-run` shows it as a blocker. Why: the service can hold the config while it changes, and on Windows a running `opencode.exe` may block the binary swap (**VERIFY**).
- `--update` no longer asks mid-run (#489): a saved OpenCode profile `none` is reused instead of showing the profile menu again, and `rtk init` runs without a terminal like every other step, so it no longer waits for an answer and its output goes to the run log. Checked with rtk 1.2.1: "Patch existing settings.json?" takes No; the "Delegate oversize reads...?" question was not seen in that run.

## [1.2.2] - 2026-11-26

### Added
- RTK now works on OpenCode 2 (#478). `--tools rtk` runs `rtk init -g --opencode` there too, as on OpenCode 1.x, and `--uninstall` removes it again. You need rtk 1.2.0 or newer; with an older or missing rtk the step is skipped and the output says how to update it.
- `--upgrade-agent opencode` keeps an `rtk.ts` that already works on OpenCode 2. For an old OpenCode 1.x-only `rtk.ts` it prints the next step, `lean-agents --update`, which rewrites the file with rtk; lean-agents never edits that file itself.
- Checked in CI on Linux and Windows with OpenCode 2.2.7 and rtk 1.2.0 (the plugin loads and rewrites a shell command). Not checked: macOS in CI, and the newer rtk 1.2.1 plugin file.

### Fixed
- `--upgrade-agent opencode` no longer drops an MCP server (for example `playwright`) or a Warp plugin that lean-agents added on OpenCode 1.x when the upgrade will not write it again. It is now kept with its own name and command, and the plan says so (#480). Machines already upgraded with 1.2.1 are not repaired automatically: copy the entry back by hand as described in `docs/migrate-opencode-v1-to-v2.md` ("If an earlier upgrade dropped a server").
- `tui.json` now follows `opencode.jsonc` for DCP (#479). When the server config ends up with lean-agents' DCP pin, an exact older or newer DCP version left in `tui.json` (for example from `opencode plugin ... --global`) moves to the same pin, so `--doctor` no longer reports a version mismatch; the output says `tui.json DCP 3.1.15 -> 3.2.0 to match opencode.jsonc` and `--uninstall` puts the old value back. A DCP version you set yourself in `opencode.jsonc` is still never changed, and then `tui.json` stays too.
- `--doctor` no longer reports "edited since install" for files that changed while one of lean-agents' own commands ran (`rtk init`, plugin installs), including files left unchanged by this run; the stored hash is refreshed only for files that changed across a command, so later user edits still show (#470).
- `--doctor`: the Antigravity IDE row is `ok` only when the app is installed (macOS app folder, Windows `winget list`); config folders alone give a `note` (#466).
- An rtk older than v1.2.0 no longer fails the install: the RTK steps are skipped with one line naming the old rtk's path and how to update it, and `--doctor` flags it (#467).

## [1.2.1] - 2026-11-25

### Added
- VS Code Insiders: with `--agents vscode-copilot`, MCP servers and strict-privacy settings are also written to the Insiders user folder when it exists, and undone by `--uninstall`; `code-insiders` counts as VS Code in detection and `--doctor`.
- OpenCode CLI spike (#428): a CI job records the real OpenCode 2 help surface, exit codes and event types for headless workers (mock LLM, no login).
- Benchmark: three long multi-step tasks (`--long`) to measure lean over long sessions (#404).
- Benchmark: `--prices in,cacheRead,cacheWrite,out` (USD per million tokens) adds a cache-aware "Priced Cost" and a median turn count to the results (#404).
- Tests: every relative link in a tracked Markdown file must point to an existing file (#437).

### Fixed
- Benchmark: a provider spend cap or auth error (HTTP 401/403, e.g. a BYOK key over its cap) now stops the run with exit 2 instead of reporting zeros as results (#404).

## [1.2.0] - 2026-11-24

### Changed
- Gemini CLI is not planned: upstream made it enterprise-only on 2026-06-18 and Antigravity CLI, already supported, covers individual accounts (#433).
- Docs: Contributor Covenant 2.1 Code of Conduct linked from CONTRIBUTING and both READMEs; roadmap 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 with the next sessions in the spec (#429).
- Docs: finished audits (2026-11, 0.8.0, 1.0.0), architecture checkpoints and `sessions-done.md` moved to `docs/archive/`; links updated. The latest release audit stays in `docs/`.
- Savings benchmark reports stable medians and a chart (#404).
- Savings benchmark: supports OpenRouter DeepSeek, multiple repeats, raw log uploads, and budget guards for runs and cost (#103).
- The Copilot usage meter in the OpenCode sidebar and the `/copilot-usage` toast now show one decimal for the percent left, truncated so it never rounds up past the real value ([#190](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/190)).
- The Claude Code `code-mode` note and the README rows now say that Remote Control, Claude in Chrome, computer use and the VS Code panel do not work while Code Mode is on, and that RTK and Context Mode do ([#304](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/304)).
- Docs: Orca facts refreshed to v1.4.274 (2026-11-24), including the moved orca.dev docs site, the mobile remote-control warning for work machines, the agent CLIs Orca 1.4.266 can install, and VERIFY marks for unconfirmed CLI and installer items.

### Added
- CI test-count guard: a pull request must not lower the test count in `tests/*.test.mjs` without an explanation in the PR body (`tests-removed: <reason>`) (#443).
- Codex CLI spike (#432): research and official upstream compatibility table for installation, config, rules, and non-interactive mode; added a GitHub workflow to test installation in a throwaway HOME.
- Groundwork, not usable yet: Code Mode proxy core with a QuickJS sandbox, allowlist and audit log in `tools/code-mode-proxy/`. Nothing in the installer uses it; `--tools code-mode-proxy` comes in 1.3.0 (#407).
- Savings benchmark can compare lean-agents rules alone with the full setup, run chosen tasks only, and measures fixed overhead per request with a one-word task (#404).
- One read-only `--doctor` row that warns when OpenCode Code Mode is turned off ([#304](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/304)).

### Fixed
- Codex CLI spike workflow: the leak check compares `npm ls -g` so the empty scope folder npm leaves after uninstall no longer fails it.
- `SECURITY.md`: 1.2.x is current; 1.1.x gets security fixes only.
- `scripts/pins-latest.mjs` refuses to run outside CI (or without `--force`), so it no longer rewrites `core/pins.json` in a normal checkout.
- Dynamic job names in CI correctly report SKIPPED on docs-only PRs, so they no longer block the merge (#371 follow-up).
- `--tools rtk` on Linux without Homebrew now installs the pinned, sha256-checked rtk release into `~/.local/bin` instead of stopping with a manual link ([#411](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/411)).
- The DCP row in `--doctor` now shows for unmanaged machines if they have an OpenCode config listing it ([#391](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/391)).
- Node version check now names a fit nvm Node to switch to, or the install command, and `--doctor` adds a "node for lean-agents" row ([#392](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/392)).
- PowerShell quoting covers typographic quotes; Cursor Windows never installs over an existing folder ([#395](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/395)).

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-23

### Added

- A reproducible savings benchmark harness for the owner to run later (`tests/bench-savings.mjs`), plus an "Active setup" line in `--doctor` and the summary page showing rules size, tools on, and subagents count ([#370](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/370)).
- `--install-agent antigravity` installs the Antigravity CLI on Windows from a sha256-pinned GitHub release, recorded and removed by `--uninstall`; the Antigravity app install is recorded with an undo ([#374](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/374)).
- `--install-agent cursor` installs the Cursor CLI on Windows from the sha256-pinned cursor.com script, recorded and removed by `--uninstall`; the Cursor app is installed with brew (macOS) or winget (Windows, user scope) only with the opt-in `--cursor-app` (`-CursorApp`) and only when missing, with a recorded undo ([#375](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/375)).
- `--add-tools a,b`: adds tools to your saved setup through `--update`, keeping the saved agents, OpenCode profile and other choices. A plain re-run now says when it would change the saved agents or profile, and `code-mode` says (in the plan and in `--doctor`) when Claude Code is older than 2.1.323 (found on a real Windows PC, [#304](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/304)).

### Changed

- Shorter README first screen and a team rollout page (docs/team-rollout.md) (#372).
- Claude Code, OpenCode 1.x and 2.x, and Cursor are now proven on macOS by scheduled CI with the real binaries (#371).
- VS Code Copilot is now proven on Windows by scheduled CI with a pinned VS Code download (#371).
- Contributor checks from #305: a test fails when install or undo code writes user files outside the `fsops` action kinds; seeded random configs must round-trip install and `--uninstall` byte for byte; the PR template and the coordinate session prompt ask for `behavior-diff.sh` output, the failing-then-passing test, and the checks a PR adds.

### Fixed

- Dry run without a terminal: takes the saved selections or defaults without asking, instead of failing with "no terminal to ask on", when stdin is not a TTY ([#393](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/393)).
- Doctor details: `mcp list` calls have a 90 s timeout and say when they timed out; missing recorded files, `npx` ECOMPROMISED failures, and DCP version mismatches each say how to fix them ([#393](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/393)).
- Release audit gate: an open audit issue labelled `release-proof` (its proof is the release run itself) no longer blocks the release; the gate prints it.
- Bun on Windows: unzip with .NET instead of Expand-Archive, which fails in Windows PowerShell started from PowerShell 7 (follow-up of #379).
- DCP is pinned in both the server and the TUI config on OpenCode 1.x and 2.x (an existing `@latest` or bare name is moved to the pin, an exact version you chose is kept), and `--doctor` shows one DCP row: registered, resolved, loads ([#212](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/212)).
- `--doctor` no longer warns about identical skill copies that lean-agents installed itself in more than one agent folder (#368).

### Security

- The manual savings benchmark workflow pins OpenCode, passes the model input through an env variable and runs with a read-only token on main only (#389).

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-20

First stable release. Highlights since 0.8.0:

- **Fresh machine:** `--everything` plans and installs the prerequisites (Node.js, git, Homebrew or winget, nvm) and the full setup from a clean Mac or Windows PC; `install.sh` and `install.ps1` work without Homebrew, Node.js, git or winget. - **OpenCode 1.x to 2.x, guided:** `--upgrade-agent opencode` backs up the 1.x sessions to a permanent frozen copy, installs 2.x next to the 1.x binary (`opencode1`), translates the config, and has an undo and a rollback ([#80](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/80)).
- **Install by VS Code Copilot agent mode:** a guide, a `--json` summary and the VS Code Copilot adapter in the agent lifecycle ([#180](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/180)).
- **Update plan and undo:** `--update --dry-run` shows what moves and the release notes, `--update` also moves the agent CLIs inside a major, and `--update --undo` restores the previous versions ([#182](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/182)).
- **Antigravity and Cursor:** Antigravity pilot (IDE and extension detection, proxy variables in `--doctor`), more pins (Antigravity cask, Bun, rtk, uv, gh), and the Cursor installer re-pinned twice.
- **Summary page:** the finish step writes a local HTML page with the log-ins to do, an agent verify prompt and next steps ([#181](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/181)).
- **CI:** macOS legs and the slow Windows legs skip pull requests (macOS runs nightly and on dispatch); the release workflow publishes to npm through trusted publishing only ([#160](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/160)).
- **Hardening:** eight independent reviews and the 0.8.0 audit are fixed or tracked in [`docs/audit-1.0.0.md`](docs/archive/audit-1.0.0.md).

### Added
- Summary page (#181 PR3, closes #181): `scripts/lib/summary-html.mjs` renders one self-contained HTML (inline CSS and JS, no network; EN and ES; light and dark; word budget tested): red Action needed (log-ins, the verify prompt with a copy button), Summary, Next steps, How to use, Updates. The finish step and `--summary` write it as an owned `summary.html` in the state dir (`--uninstall` removes it) and print its path; the browser opens only after a yes, never under CI, `--yes`, `--json` or `--no-open`. `--filed-issue "item=issue url"` records an issue the verify prompt filed.
- `--tools code-mode` (opt-in, never in `--all-tools`): sets `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1` in the user `env` of `~/.claude/settings.json` when it is not set, and prints the limits: experimental, Claude Code 2.1.323+, interactive terminal, direct Anthropic login, sessions resume only with it on. `--uninstall` removes it ([#304](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/304)).
- `docs/vscode-agent-checklist.md` (#180 PR5, docs only): one-time manual checklist for a real work PC (VS Code Copilot agent mode behind a proxy): paste the prompt, answers, blocked terminal tool, `--doctor`, undo, and the exact `compatibility.md` VERIFY row each step moves, with the fields to record.
- `--update --undo [--yes]` (#278): reinstalls the saved previous version of each agent CLI that `--update` upgraded, using the oldest `from` per agent (two upgrades 1.0 -> 1.1 -> 1.2 end on 1.0, not 1.1). Plan first, then a confirm (or `--yes`); a failed step is reported (exit 1) and the rest continue; restored agents' records leave `state.json`, a failed one keeps its record for a retry. `--uninstall` still leaves upgraded agent CLIs alone. Tests in `tests/agent-upgrade.test.mjs` (stubbed `claude`, `curl` and `npm`: a failing installer keeps `from`/`reinstall`, later steps run, undo ends on the oldest version).
- Agent CLI upgrades within a major (#182 PR3): after the `--update` confirm, Claude Code (pinned installer with the version argument), OpenCode 2 (installer `--version`) and Copilot CLI (`npm install -g @github/copilot@<pin>`) that lean-agents installed move to the release pin (`upgradeCommands` in `agent-lifecycle.mjs`). Never OpenCode 1.x, another major, an agent you installed yourself or the VS Code Copilot extension; Cursor and Antigravity have no pin and are not moved. Each command is saved in `state.json` with `from` and `reinstall` (the installer at the previous version; `--update --undo` runs it, see below); `--uninstall` ignores it. A failed step is reported and the rest continue. The plan row for these agents is now `update` instead of `report`. Tests in `tests/agent-upgrade.test.mjs`.
- Summary data model and login checks (#181 PR1, internal, no flag yet): `scripts/lib/summary-data.mjs` builds the finish-step summary (installed, kept, updated, skipped, doctor result, login checklist) from state, doctor rows and the `--json` apply shape, every text through `redactText`; `scripts/lib/logins.mjs` lists the login command per tool and checks `gh auth status` and `claude auth status` by exit code only (never under `--no-exec` or outbound off, output dropped, credentials never read).
- Agent self-updaters off for every managed install (#182 PR5): Claude Code `env.DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`, OpenCode 2 `update: "disable"`, OpenCode 1 `autoupdate: false` and Copilot CLI `autoUpdate: false` are now written whatever the network preset (before: only with auto-updates off), as `setIfAbsent` so a value you set is kept and reported, forced only when the category is off; `--uninstall` removes them. `--update` is the one way agents get updated. Cursor and Antigravity document no switch (**VERIFY**), so they are untouched.
- Verify prompt and feedback flow (#181 PR2): `scripts/lib/verify-prompt.mjs` (EN/ES; doctor, fix within the plan, redacted draft, duplicate search, `gh issue create` only after a per-issue yes, links written back; no filing text under strict or `--network off`), `draftFromRow` and the `filedIssues` record in `scripts/lib/feedback.mjs`, `--feedback-kind verify`, docs in `install-with-an-agent.md` and `privacy.md`. Wired into `--summary` by PR3.
- `lean-update` skill and N-1 -> N proof (#182 PR6): the skill now plans with `--update --dry-run`, asks, applies, reads back with `--doctor` and hands off to the finish-step summary page (#181) when the release has it; its backup and cleanup snippets are Node one-liners that run unchanged in bash and PowerShell. `tests/skill-flags.test.mjs` checks every `--flag` in the skill against `--help`. `tests/real-update.sh` adds, only when `CI_LATEST` is true (nightly/dispatch), an install from the last published release's pins, `--update --yes`, `--doctor` and a clean `--uninstall`; no new CI job.
- Agent CLI upgrades within a major (#182 PR3): after the `--update` confirm, Claude Code (pinned installer with the version argument), OpenCode 2 (installer `--version`) and Copilot CLI (`npm install -g @github/copilot@<pin>`) that lean-agents installed move to the release pin (`upgradeCommands` in `agent-lifecycle.mjs`). # Changelog

All notable changes are documented here. Format: [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/). Versioning: [SemVer](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

## [1.2.5] - 2026-11-27

### Added
- `scripts/release-gate.sh <version> [sha]` runs the release gate (audit headings, open `audit` issues, green `ci.yml` run) locally, and `release.yml` calls it instead of inline steps (#515).
- Changelog fragments: each PR adds `changes/<issue>.md`; `node scripts/changelog.mjs <version>` folds them into `CHANGELOG.md` in the release PR, so parallel PRs no longer conflict under `## [Unreleased]` (#516).

### Changed
- `core/AGENTS.md` trimmed from 3,016 to 1,599 bytes; every 1.2.4 safety rule kept (#532)

### Docs
- `docs/audit-template.md` with the headings a release audit must have (#515)

### Fixed
- Real-binary CI downloads retry a 5xx three times before failing (#505)
- `--adopt` and `--upgrade-agent` shorten a Windows home path to `~` whatever its letter case, and `tilde()` no longer matches a home inside a longer path (#506)

## [1.2.4] - 2026-11-27

### Added
- `--adopt` (and `--adopt --json`) now lists every global npm package under every Node nvm knows, not only the npm packages lean-agents pins (#465). The active/default Node is marked, and a package is flagged when it exists only under another Node (`not-active`), sits under several Nodes at different versions (`version-differs`) or does not meet its own `engines.node` on the Node it lives under (`engines-unmet`). Cleanup is one `npm uninstall -g <pkg> --prefix <Node dir>` line per package only on a non-active Node: printed, never run, and not part of the `--yes` plan. The `--adopt --json` shape is in `docs/adopt-json.md`. nvm-windows stays **VERIFY**. Not done yet: flagging MCP/hook entries on a non-active Node and listing Node installs outside nvm on PATH.
- Multi-agent benchmark harness (#404): `tests/bench-multiagent.mjs` runs task9 solo or split across 1, 2 or 4 workers plus one reviewer, records per-session tokens and wall time, and reports priced cost and cost versus solo. It has a `--dry-run` plan, a hard USD cap, and a manual-only workflow.

### Fixed
- The Claude Code `context-mode` plugin pin moved from `v2.1.4` to `v2.1.7`, matching the npm CLI that `--update` already installs (#490). A new test fails when the two pins drift apart without a `note` on the plugin pin explaining why.
- The skipped `real-vscode-others` job no longer shows an unexpanded `real-vscode (${{ matrix.os }})` name in the checks list (#460). It has no custom name now, so a skip should show `real-vscode-others` and a real run still shows one job per OS.
- `--doctor` clears a stale `~/.claude/settings.json` hash left by 1.2.1, when the only difference is keys lean-agents' own `claude plugin` commands wrote (`enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`): `--update` now refreshes the stored hash for tracked JSON files whose command-written key paths it knows, even when the file did not change in that run (#492). A key lean-agents does not write still shows "edited since install".

## [1.2.3] - 2026-11-26

### Changed
- Quieter output (#491): each install or `--update` step prints one line `[n/N] description ✓` (or `✗` with the last 20 lines and the log path); the commands' own output goes to one log per run in `~/.config/lean-agents/logs/` (removed by `--uninstall`), so a child's stderr no longer shows red in PowerShell on a good run. The plan lists only `create`/`modify`/`remove` files plus one `N unchanged` line, release notes show the first sentence of each entry plus the CHANGELOG link, and command lines print the home as `~`. `--verbose` restores the full output; `--json` is unchanged. Child commands get no stdin, so a tool that asks a question takes its default instead of waiting (#489).

### Added
- `--preflight` (and `--preflight --json`) is a read-only check for old or duplicate copies of the agent CLIs and tools on PATH and for a terminal opened before a PATH change (#471). It lists every copy and which one wins, and gives one fix line per finding. Blockers (exit 1): rtk below its minimum version (its steps are skipped), a newer copy hidden behind an older one, a tool this window cannot see yet. Everything else, such as an older copy later on PATH, uv, jq or gh below their verified version, or a CLI behind its pinned version, is a warning. It only runs `--version` (and `reg.exe query` on Windows); `--no-exec` skips both. It also lists the OpenCode MCP server names (your own as `<user-mcp-N>`, so the report can be shared), warns when a pinned npm tool sits under several nvm Nodes or only under an inactive one (#465), and blocks when the disk is too small for the OpenCode 1.x backup or an OpenCode process is running (#488). jq and the other tools get a package-manager fix line.

### Fixed
- `--adopt` no longer marks a skill as `duplicate` when lean-agents installed it and every copy is the same (#477), for example `lean-update` after an install for Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code Copilot, or `orca-cli` with `--terminal orca`. The Skills CLI writes one copy per agent folder on purpose. So `--adopt --yes --confirm-removals` no longer offers to remove those copies. Copies that differ, or a skill from a failed install, are still flagged. `--doctor` already worked this way.
- The Copilot CLI context-mode step no longer uses a `context-mode` copy in the current folder. That happened when `npm root -g` failed. It now uses only absolute paths and otherwise stops with the "not found" message.
- `--feedback-draft` titles say "Problem running: …" instead of "Install failed" (the input can be a warning from a command that exited 0), and a long title ends on a whole word with `…` (#476). Package specs such as `lean-agents@1.2.1` stay in the draft (fixed by the redaction change in #491; now tested).
- Child processes no longer run in shell mode (#475, Node 24 warning DEP0190). Arguments with a space, `&`, `%` or `|` now reach the program unchanged, Windows npm and npx included (their `.cmd` files run through `cmd.exe` with each argument quoted, as cross-spawn does it).
- `--doctor` and the step lines no longer print your full Windows home path when a path uses another letter case than the home folder (`c:\Users\...` for Copilot files, #493): it shows `~\...` like every other row, so pasted output does not carry your username. macOS and Linux stay case-sensitive.
- `--doctor`'s DCP row reads OpenCode 2.2.7's plugin cache (`~/.cache/opencode/npm/<pkg>@<spec>/<id>/`), so it no longer shows an old `resolved` version and a false "changed" while the pinned DCP loads fine (#495). `--doctor --probe-plugins` copies only what the probe needs (not the config's `node_modules` or wrappers of specs the config no longer asks for), so it no longer stops at the size cap on a long-used cache.
- `--update` refuses to start, and changes nothing, when its plan touches OpenCode (the CLI upgrade, `rtk init --opencode`, the GSD install for OpenCode) while an `opencode` process runs: the 1.x app or the 2.x background service. It says to run `opencode service stop` first (#488). `--dry-run` shows it as a blocker. Why: the service can hold the config while it changes, and on Windows a running `opencode.exe` may block the binary swap (**VERIFY**).
- `--update` no longer asks mid-run (#489): a saved OpenCode profile `none` is reused instead of showing the profile menu again, and `rtk init` runs without a terminal like every other step, so it no longer waits for an answer and its output goes to the run log. Checked with rtk 1.2.1: "Patch existing settings.json?" takes No; the "Delegate oversize reads...?" question was not seen in that run.

## [1.2.2] - 2026-11-26

### Added
- RTK now works on OpenCode 2 (#478). `--tools rtk` runs `rtk init -g --opencode` there too, as on OpenCode 1.x, and `--uninstall` removes it again. You need rtk 1.2.0 or newer; with an older or missing rtk the step is skipped and the output says how to update it.
- `--upgrade-agent opencode` keeps an `rtk.ts` that already works on OpenCode 2. For an old OpenCode 1.x-only `rtk.ts` it prints the next step, `lean-agents --update`, which rewrites the file with rtk; lean-agents never edits that file itself.
- Checked in CI on Linux and Windows with OpenCode 2.2.7 and rtk 1.2.0 (the plugin loads and rewrites a shell command). Not checked: macOS in CI, and the newer rtk 1.2.1 plugin file.

### Fixed
- `--upgrade-agent opencode` no longer drops an MCP server (for example `playwright`) or a Warp plugin that lean-agents added on OpenCode 1.x when the upgrade will not write it again. It is now kept with its own name and command, and the plan says so (#480). Machines already upgraded with 1.2.1 are not repaired automatically: copy the entry back by hand as described in `docs/migrate-opencode-v1-to-v2.md` ("If an earlier upgrade dropped a server").
- `tui.json` now follows `opencode.jsonc` for DCP (#479). When the server config ends up with lean-agents' DCP pin, an exact older or newer DCP version left in `tui.json` (for example from `opencode plugin ... --global`) moves to the same pin, so `--doctor` no longer reports a version mismatch; the output says `tui.json DCP 3.1.15 -> 3.2.0 to match opencode.jsonc` and `--uninstall` puts the old value back. A DCP version you set yourself in `opencode.jsonc` is still never changed, and then `tui.json` stays too.
- `--doctor` no longer reports "edited since install" for files that changed while one of lean-agents' own commands ran (`rtk init`, plugin installs), including files left unchanged by this run; the stored hash is refreshed only for files that changed across a command, so later user edits still show (#470).
- `--doctor`: the Antigravity IDE row is `ok` only when the app is installed (macOS app folder, Windows `winget list`); config folders alone give a `note` (#466).
- An rtk older than v1.2.0 no longer fails the install: the RTK steps are skipped with one line naming the old rtk's path and how to update it, and `--doctor` flags it (#467).
- README (EN, ES): the Antigravity pilot section no longer says lean-agents skips the IDE; it installs it with Homebrew or winget unless `--no-app`.

- `--doctor` no longer warns about identical skill copies that lean-agents installed itself in more than one agent folder (#368).

### Security

- The manual savings benchmark workflow pins OpenCode, passes the model input through an env variable and runs with a read-only token on main only (#389).

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-20

First stable release. Highlights since 0.8.0:

- **Fresh machine:** `--everything` plans and installs the prerequisites (Node.js, git, Homebrew or winget, nvm) and the full setup from a clean Mac or Windows PC; `install.sh` and `install.ps1` work without Homebrew, Node.js, git or winget. A nightly workflow runs it ([#179](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/179)).
- **OpenCode 1.x to 2.x, guided:** `--upgrade-agent opencode` backs up the 1.x sessions to a permanent frozen copy, installs 2.x next to the 1.x binary (`opencode1`), translates the config, and has an undo and a rollback ([#80](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/80)).
- **Install by VS Code Copilot agent mode:** a guide, a `--json` summary and the VS Code Copilot adapter in the agent lifecycle ([#180](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/180)).
- **Update plan and undo:** `--update --dry-run` shows what moves and the release notes, `--update` also moves the agent CLIs inside a major, and `--update --undo` restores the previous versions ([#182](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/182)).
- **Antigravity and Cursor:** Antigravity pilot (IDE and extension detection, proxy variables in `--doctor`), more pins (Antigravity cask, Bun, rtk, uv, gh), and the Cursor installer re-pinned twice.
- **Summary page:** the finish step writes a local HTML page with the log-ins to do, an agent verify prompt and next steps ([#181](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/181)).
- **CI:** macOS legs and the slow Windows legs skip pull requests (macOS runs nightly and on dispatch); the release workflow publishes to npm through trusted publishing only ([#160](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/160)).
- **Hardening:** eight independent reviews and the 0.8.0 audit are fixed or tracked in [`docs/audit-1.0.0.md`](docs/archive/audit-1.0.0.md).

### Added
- Summary page (#181 PR3, closes #181): `scripts/lib/summary-html.mjs` renders one self-contained HTML (inline CSS and JS, no network; EN and ES; light and dark; word budget tested): red Action needed (log-ins, the verify prompt with a copy button), Summary, Next steps, How to use, Updates. The finish step and `--summary` write it as an owned `summary.html` in the state dir (`--uninstall` removes it) and print its path; the browser opens only after a yes, never under CI, `--yes`, `--json` or `--no-open`. `--filed-issue "item=issue url"` records an issue the verify prompt filed.
- `--tools code-mode` (opt-in, never in `--all-tools`): sets `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1` in the user `env` of `~/.claude/settings.json` when it is not set, and prints the limits: experimental, Claude Code 2.1.323+, interactive terminal, direct Anthropic login, sessions resume only with it on. `--uninstall` removes it ([#304](https://github.com/estebanmr99/lean-agents/issues/304)).
- `docs/vscode-agent-checklist.md` (#180 PR5, docs only): one-time manual checklist for a real work PC (VS Code Copilot agent mode behind a proxy): paste the prompt, answers, blocked terminal tool, `--doctor`, undo, and the exact `compatibility.md` VERIFY row each step moves, with the fields to record.
- `--update --undo [--yes]` (#278): reinstalls the saved previous version of each agent CLI that `--update` upgraded, using the oldest `from` per agent (two upgrades 1.0 -> 1.1 -> 1.2 end on 1.0, not 1.1). Plan first, then a confirm (or `--yes`); a failed step is reported (exit 1) and the rest continue; restored agents' records leave `state.json`, a failed one keeps its record for a retry. `--uninstall` still leaves upgraded agent CLIs alone. Tests in `tests/agent-upgrade.test.mjs` (stubbed `claude`, `curl` and `npm`: a failing installer keeps `from`/`reinstall`, later steps run, undo ends on the oldest version).
- Agent CLI upgrades within a major (#182 PR3): after the `--update` confirm, Claude Code (pinned installer with the version argument), OpenCode 2 (installer `--version`) and Copilot CLI (`npm install -g @github/copilot@<pin>`) that lean-agents installed move to the release pin (`upgradeCommands` in `agent-lifecycle.mjs`). Never OpenCode 1.x, another major, an agent you installed yourself or the VS Code Copilot extension; Cursor and Antigravity have no pin and are not moved. Each command is saved in `state.json` with `from` and `reinstall` (the installer at the previous version; `--update --undo` runs it, see below); `--uninstall` ignores it. A failed step is reported and the rest continue. The plan row for these agents is now `update` instead of `report`. Tests in `tests/agent-upgrade.test.mjs`.
- Summary data model and login checks (#181 PR1, internal, no flag yet): `scripts/lib/summary-data.mjs` builds the finish-step summary (installed, kept, updated, skipped, doctor result, login checklist) from state, doctor rows and the `--json` apply shape, every text through `redactText`; `scripts/lib/logins.mjs` lists the login command per tool and checks `gh auth status` and `claude auth status` by exit code only (never under `--no-exec` or outbound off, output dropped, credentials never read).
- Agent self-updaters off for every managed install (#182 PR5): Claude Code `env.DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`, OpenCode 2 `update: "disable"`, OpenCode 1 `autoupdate: false` and Copilot CLI `autoUpdate: false` are now written whatever the network preset (before: only with auto-updates off), as `setIfAbsent` so a value you set is kept and reported, forced only when the category is off; `--uninstall` removes them. `--update` is the one way agents get updated. Cursor and Antigravity document no switch (**VERIFY**), so they are untouched.
- Verify prompt and feedback flow (#181 PR2): `scripts/lib/verify-prompt.mjs` (EN/ES; doctor, fix within the plan, redacted draft, duplicate search, `gh issue create` only after a per-issue yes, links written back; no filing text under strict or `--network off`), `draftFromRow` and the `filedIssues` record in `scripts/lib/feedback.mjs`, `--feedback-kind verify`, docs in `install-with-an-agent.md` and `privacy.md`. Wired into `--summary` by PR3.
- `lean-update` skill and N-1 -> N proof (#182 PR6): the skill now plans with `--update --dry-run`, asks, applies, reads back with `--doctor` and hands off to the finish-step summary page (#181) when the release has it; its backup and cleanup snippets are Node one-liners that run unchanged in bash and PowerShell. `tests/skill-flags.test.mjs` checks every `--flag` in the skill against `--help`. `tests/real-update.sh` adds, only when `CI_LATEST` is true (nightly/dispatch), an install from the last published release's pins, `--update --yes`, `--doctor` and a clean `--uninstall`; no new CI job.
- Agent CLI upgrades within a major (#182 PR3): after the `--update` confirm, Claude Code (pinned installer with the version argument), OpenCode 2 (installer `--version`) and Copilot CLI (`npm install -g @github/copilot@<pin>`) that lean-agents installed move to the release pin (`upgradeCommands` in `agent-lifecycle.mjs`). Never OpenCode 1.x, another major, an agent you installed yourself or the VS Code Copilot extension; Cursor and Antigravity have no pin and are not moved. Each command is saved in `state.json` with `from` and `reinstall` (the installer at the previous version; `undoUpgrades()` runs it, no flag yet); `--uninstall` ignores it.
